action.description: One of 'publish', 'list', 'read', 'delete', 'open', 'pin', 'unpin', 'quickstart'. Omitting it means 'publish'. **Calls** in the description says what each one does and takes, except as noted here.

file_path.description: publish: the local page Claude publishes (.html, or .md only when a skill says so). For an Artifact created from an Artifact type, it is one of that Artifact's data files. With `asset: true`, it is the local file Claude uploads. A short, distinctive basename also serves as the title when nothing else gives one.

asset.description: publish with `url`: true uploads `file_path` (or each of `file_paths`) to that artifact's asset store instead of publishing it as the page — or, with `from_url` and `asset_ids` in place of `file_path`, copies those assets of another artifact into it server side (see **Calls**).

file_paths.description: publish with `asset: true` only: several local image, video, PDF, font, stylesheet or script files in place of `file_path`, up to 25 in one call, all into the artifact that `url` names; one approval covers the call, and the result lists each file's id and url, or why it was not uploaded. A CSV, Markdown, JSON or plain-text file, a symbolic or hard link, and a file outside the working directory each go in a call of their own with `file_path`.

from_url.description: publish with `asset: true`, in place of `file_path`: the SOURCE artifact's claude.ai URL — one the person can open.

asset_ids.description: publish with `asset: true` and `from_url` only: 1–10 distinct asset ids from the source artifact (from a `scope: "assets"` listing of it, or an upload result).

favicon.description: Deprecated; Claude omits it and uses `icon`.

icon.description: One short generic word for the artifact's browser-tab icon, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map: a plain signifier, never a product or brand name. Claude includes it on every page's first publish and omits it on a redeploy so the artifact keeps its icon, passing a new one only when the person asks. Ignored on an Artifact created from an Artifact type.

files.description: Supporting files to publish alongside the page, as a map {"published/path": "source/path" | {from, contentType} | {artifact, path, ver?} | null}. The key is what the HTML references. The source is a path on disk, or {from, contentType} when the type cannot be inferred from the published extension. An {artifact, path} source copies that Artifact's published file on the server: an Artifact the person can open, with its type carried over, never an HTML or XML document, and at most 4 source Artifact versions per publish. null removes that path on an update, and files left out are kept. A plain list publishes each file at its own spelling. Sources must be under the working directory or Claude's scratchpad directory. `preflight.js` at the artifact root is reserved: it runs against open pages when Claude publishes updates, and it must be a JavaScript module of at most 8 KiB whose default export is a function, or the publish is refused.

path.description: Path relative to the working directory (or to `root`, which may be a folder in your scratchpad directory); the file is served at this same path next to the page.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the extension for common types (css/js/json/png/…) — pass explicitly otherwise.

from.description: Source file path — relative to `root` (default: the working directory), or absolute under the working directory or your scratchpad directory.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the PUBLISHED extension for common types — pass explicitly otherwise.

artifact.description: Another artifact's claude.ai URL: the file is copied from ITS published files, server side — nothing is downloaded. You must be able to open that artifact.

path.description: The file's published path inside that Artifact, as a listing of its files prints it (not "index.html").

ver.description: A version of that Artifact to copy from instead of its current one — only versions you are served (its history, if you can edit it); omit for the current version.

edits.description: publish: small changes Claude makes to the file at `file_path` in this same call, instead of editing the file with Edit and publishing after. Use it on a page (add `url` to update an artifact from another conversation) or on one data file of an artifact made from a type (its `url`, with that file as `file_path`). Not allowed with `type_url` or `files`. Each old_str is text copied exactly from the file as it now stands and must occur in it exactly once; new_str takes its place (empty deletes it). The edits apply in order, all or none: the file is published with them and then saved with them on disk, so it stays the source for later changes; on a miss nothing is changed or published, and the result says which edit failed and why.

old_str.description: Text copied exactly from the file; must occur once.

root.description: The base directory that relative `files` sources resolve against, like a bundler root. It never changes published paths. It is relative to the working directory, or absolute within it or within Claude's scratchpad directory. It requires `files`, except on an Artifact made from a type, where a data `file_path` under it is served at its path relative to it.

pin.description: publish only: true also pins the published artifact to the person's claude.ai sidebar once it is published. Claude passes it only when the person asked for that. A failed pin never fails the publish, and the result says so.

limit.description: list only: the maximum number of artifacts to return (default 25).

scope.description: list: which listing to return. 'mine' is the default. The others are 'shared', 'all', 'types', 'files' (with `url`) and 'assets' (with `url`, continued with `after`). See **Calls**.

type_query.description: list with scope 'types' only: limits the listing to the types whose title or description match this text best, ignoring case; a type that matches less well is left out, so a narrowed listing is not the whole catalog. Claude omits it when choosing a type for a request, unless a listing made without it says more types exist than it shows.

type.description: list only: the name of a published Artifact type, as a 'types' listing shows it (case does not matter). The listing then shows the Artifacts made from that type instead of the person's gallery. Claude passes this or `type_url`, not both.

intent.description: quickstart only (required): what is being made — 'document' (text to read or edit together), 'slides' (a deck or one slide), 'design' (a visual design or prototype on a canvas), 'other' (a dashboard that shows data, anything else, or unsure).

design_systems.description: quickstart only: false when a design system's link is already in hand (it is then read with its own call) or one was declined. Omitted or true, the result lists the design systems (not for a document) and, for slides or a design, attaches the default one's README.

title.description: publish: the fallback title for an HTML page whose file has no <title>. It is a name, not a summary, and Claude keeps it the same across redeploys. On a `type_url` create, it is the new Artifact's name: what the person called it, or a short descriptive name. If it is left out, the Artifact is named after the type.

description.description: publish: one sentence for the subtitle on the gallery card.

label.description: A short name for this publish, at most 60 characters (e.g. "Draft to legal"). Optional. It is a few words, not a description.

overwrite_unread.description: publish with `files` or `root` to an existing artifact: published paths this call may replace or remove although you have not read or listed them in this session. Every other path the call touches must be one you read by its `path`, saw in a file listing, or published yourself, and must not have changed since — otherwise nothing is sent and the refusal names each path. Name a path here only when the user asked for it to be replaced without looking at what is there; it never excuses a path that changed after you read it.

url.description: An existing artifact's claude.ai link (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}); a chat, project or session link is not one, and `action: "list"` lists the person's artifacts. On a publish, it is the artifact to update in place, one the person owns or was given edit access to (a read of it says "writer"). Before publishing to an artifact this conversation has neither read nor published, Claude reads it (`action: "read"`) and builds on what comes back; a publish sent without that read is refused. A refusal that hands Claude the live version counts as that read: Claude merges its changes into that version and publishes the result, and never resends the refused content unchanged. Claude omits `url` for a new artifact or to redeploy a file this conversation already published. For read, delete and the other calls that take a URL, it is the artifact to act on.

type_url.description: publish: the Artifact type to create this new, private Artifact from (a link from a 'types' listing). Claude omits `url`. Any `file_path`/`files` passed become the new Artifact's own files beside the type's fixed ones. read (no `url`): the type to describe. list: the type whose Artifacts to list, or Claude names the type with `type` instead.

auto_open.description: Only with `type_url` and no `file_path`: when the new Artifact opens for the person. Claude passes "after_first_write" when it will fill the Artifact right after creating it with a files publish to its url, so the person does not first see it empty. The Artifact then opens on that first write. Otherwise Claude omits it, and the Artifact opens when created; Claude always omits it for a type whose content it writes through a connector, such as a Claude Docs document, since no publish or store write follows to open it.

prompt.description: read, for an artifact shared with the person: what Claude needs from it, which steers the isolated summary.

force.description: publish: a last-resort overwrite that **discards** the newer published version. On a conflict, Claude merges its changes onto the newer content that the rejection hands it and publishes again. Claude passes true only when the person explicitly said to discard that specific version, and the server may still refuse it over a version saved from inside the page.

out_dir.description: read with `path`: the directory to save into. The default is this artifact's folder in Claude's scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval. A published file lands at <out_dir>/<published path>, and saving it outside that default folder asks the person first. An asset's file is named by its id plus its type's extension; saving it outside the default folder is an ordinary file save the person may be asked to approve.

path.description: read: the file's published path inside the artifact, exactly as a 'files' listing printed it ("index.html" is the page itself). The file is saved locally, the result says where, and a small text file's contents are included. It can instead be an uploaded asset's id (32 hex characters, from an 'assets' listing or an upload result), and that asset is saved to a local file. delete: the id of the one asset to remove.

paths.description: read: several published paths in place of `path`, up to 256 in one call. Each file is saved as a single `path` would be, and the result lists where each one landed, or why it could not be read, with small text files' contents included while they fit.

after.description: list with scope 'assets' only: the `next` value from a previous listing, passed to continue it.

page.description: read only: true returns the rendered page in cases where a read otherwise returns something else. A typed Artifact's read leaves out the type's own page.

capabilities.description: publish: the runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. Claude loads the `artifact-capabilities` skill before passing it. On a redeploy Claude omits the field to keep what the page has, and {} clears it.

contract.description: publish: the artifact's runtime version. Leaving it out keeps the current version (the default), 'latest' upgrades, and an exact version pins or rolls back. It changes how the published page behaves, so Claude passes it only when the author explicitly intends that change.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task.

If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

items.description: The whole plan, in order (1–12 steps); replaces the previous list.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

FILE SESSION:
Once the target fileKey is known, call create_session with that key and a concise task description before search_design_system, get_libraries, use_figma, or any other file tool. This applies to read-only tasks too. If a new file is needed, call create_new_file first, then create_session with the returned file key. Reuse the returned UUID as the sessionId argument on eligible file tools for subsequent work on that task, including calls to other files.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skil

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

FILE SESSION:
Once the target fileKey is known, call create_session with that key and a concise task description before search_design_system, get_libraries, use_figma, or any other file tool. This applies to read-only tasks too. If a new file is needed, call create_new_file first, then create_session with the returned file key. Reuse the returned UUID as the sessionId argument on eligible file tools for subsequent work on that task, including calls to other files.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Retrieval regression probe for Entire Brain.
3	
4	Builds an isolated brain store from a committed fixture, runs the labeled
5	`memories eval` facts retriever and a `brief` packet probe against it, and
6	compares the branch binary with the base-branch binary. The result is a
7	0-100 trail monitor value plus a one-line rationale.
8	
9	This is a regression signal, not evidence. See README.md for what it does
10	and does not claim.
11	
12	Subcommands:
13	  freeze   seed the fixture with one binary and write fixture/tasks.json
14	  measure  seed + eval + brief probe for one binary, print the report
15	  compare  build HEAD and a base ref, measure both, print report and monitor
16	"""
17	
18	from __future__ import annotations
19	
20	import argparse
21	import hashlib
22	import json
23	import os
24	import shutil
25	import subprocess
26	import sys
27	import tempfile
28	from pathlib import Path
29	from typing import Any
30	
31	HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
32	FIXTURE_DIR = HERE / "fixture"
33	FACTS_PATH = FIXTURE_DIR / "facts.json"
34	QUESTIONS_PATH = FIXTURE_DIR / "questions.json"
35	TASKS_PATH = FIXTURE_DIR / "tasks.json"
36	
37	# A brief packet whose facts key sits past this fraction of the bytes is the
38	# #335 shape: a status block ahead of the evidence, which truncating agents
39	# never reach.
40	BRIEF_PREFIX_LIMIT = 0.5
41	
42	
43	class ProbeError(RuntimeError):
44	    """A step that makes the measurement meaningless (build, seed, contract)."""
45	
46	
47	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
48	# helpers
49	
50	
51	def sha256_file(path: Path) -> str:
52	    return "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
53	
54	
55	def load_json(path: Path) -> Any:
56	    with path.open(encoding="utf-8") as fh:
57	        return json.load(fh)
58	
59	
60	def run(argv: list[str], *, cwd: Path, env: dict[str, str], timeout: int = 300) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
61	    return subprocess.run(
62	        argv,
63	        cwd=str(cwd),
64	        env=env,
65	        capture_output=True,
66	        text=True,
67	        timeout=timeout,
68	        check=False,
69	    )
70	
71	
72	def git_env(base: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, str]:
73	    """Git with no user or system config: no hooks, no entire checkpoints."""
74	    env = dict(base)
75	    env["GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL"] = os.devnull
76	    env["GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM"] = os.devnull
77	    env["GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT"] = "0"
78	    return env
79	
80	
81	def repo_root() -> Path:
82	    out = subprocess.run(
83	        ["git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"],
84	        cwd=str(HERE),
85	        capture_output=True,
86	        text=True,
87	        check=True,
88	    )
89	    return Path(out.stdout.strip())
90	
91	
92	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
93	# isolated store
94	
95	
96	class FixtureStore:
97	    """A throwaway repository plus plugin dirs that one binary writes into."""
98	
99	    def __init__(self, root: Path, origin: str, branch: str) -> None:
100	        self.root = root
101	        self.repo = root / "repo"
102	        self.xdg = root / "xdg"
103	        self.origin = origin
104	        self.branch = branch
105	
106	    def create(self) -> None:
107	        self.repo.mkdir(parents=True)
108	        for name in ("config", "data", "state", "cache"):
109	            (self.xdg / name).mkdir(parents=True)
110	        env = git_env(os.environ.copy())
111	        steps = [
112	            ["git", "init", "-q", "-b", self.branch],
113	            ["git", "remote", "add", "origin", self.origin],
114	            [
115	                "git",
116	                "-c",
117	                "user.name=fixture",
118	                "-c",
119	                "user.email=fixture@example.invalid",
120	                "commit",
121	                "-q",
122	                "--allow-empty",
123	                "-m",
124	                "retrieval regression fixture",
125	            ],
126	        ]
127	        for argv in steps:
128	            proc = run(argv, cwd=self.repo, env=env)
129	            if proc.returncode != 0:
130	                raise ProbeError(f"fixture git step failed: {' '.join(argv)}: {proc.stderr.strip()}")
131	
132	    def env(self) -> dict[str, str]:
133	        env = git_env(os.environ.copy())
134	        env["ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT"] = str(self.repo)
135	        env["ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CONFIG_DIR"] = str(self.xdg / "config")
136	        env["ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR"] = str(self.xdg / "data")
137	        env["ENTIRE_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR"] = str(self.xdg / "state")
138	        env["ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR"] = str(self.xdg / "cache")
139	        env.pop("ENTIRE_BRAIN_SESSION_ID", None)
140	        return env
141	
142	    def brain(self, binary: Path, *args: str, timeout: int = 120) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
143	        return run([str(binary), *args], cwd=self.repo, env=self.env(), timeout=timeout)
144	
145	
146	def seed(store: FixtureStore, binary: Path, facts: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, str]:
147	    """Record every fixture fact; return key -> fact id."""
148	    ids: dict[str, str] = {}
149	    for fact in facts["facts"]:
150	        proc = store.brain(
151	            binary,
152	            "remember",
153	            fact["text"],
154	            "--path",
155	            fact["path"],
156	            "--kind",
157	            fact["kind"],
158	            "--branch",
159	            store.branch,
160	            "--agent",
161	            "none",
162	            "--json",
163	        )
164	        if proc.returncode != 0:
165	            raise ProbeError(f"remember failed for {fact['key']}: {proc.stderr.strip()[:300]}")
166	        try:
167	            payload = json.loads(proc.stdout)
168	        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
169	            raise ProbeError(f"remember emitted no JSON for {fact['key']}: {exc}") from exc
170	        fact_id = str(payload.get("id") or "").strip()
171	        if not fact_id:
172	            raise ProbeError(f"remember returned no id for {fact['key']}")
173	        ids[fact["key"]] = fact_id
174	    return ids
175	
176	
177	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
178	# measurement
179	
180	
181	def mean_recall(summary: dict[str, Any]) -> float:
182	    labeled = [r for r in summary.get("results") or [] if r.get("labeled")]
183	    return (sum(float(r.get("recall", 0.0)) for r in labeled) / len(labeled)) if labeled else 0.0
184	
185	
186	def top_rank_tasks(tasks: list[dict[str, Any]], out_path: Path) -> Path:
187	    """The same tasks with k = number of labels: recall is then 1 only when every
188	    labeled fact outranks every distractor. Precision at a fixed k is pinned near
189	    1/k and says nothing about ranking; this does."""
190	    tight = [dict(t, k=max(1, len(t["relevant"]))) for t in tasks]
191	    out_path.write_text(json.dumps(tight), encoding="utf-8")
192	    return out_path
193	
194	
195	def eval_facts(store: FixtureStore, binary: Path, tasks_path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
196	    proc = store.brain(
197	        binary,
198	        "memories",
199	        "eval",
200	        "--tasks",
201	        str(tasks_path),
202	        "--retriever",
203	        "facts",
204	        "--branch",
205	        store.branch,
206	        "--agent",
207	        "none",
208	        "--json",
209	        timeout=300,
210	    )
211	    if proc.returncode != 0:
212	        raise ProbeError(f"memories eval failed: {proc.stderr.strip()[:300]}")
213	    try:
214	        return json.loads(proc.stdout)
215	    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
216	        raise ProbeError(f"memories eval emitted no JSON: {exc}") from exc
217	
218	
219	def brief_probe(store: FixtureStore, binary: Path, tasks: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
220	    """Does the brief packet carry the labeled facts, and how far in do they sit?"""
221	    rows = []
222	    for task in tasks:
223	        proc = store.brain(binary, "brief", task["task"], "--json")
224	        raw = proc.stdout
225	        row: dict[str, Any] = {"id": task["id"], "ok": proc.returncode == 0, "bytes": len(raw.encode("utf-8"))}
226	        if proc.returncode != 0:
227	            row["error"] = proc.stderr.strip()[:200]
228	            row["hit"] = False
229	            row["prefix_fraction"] = 1.0
230	            rows.append(row)
231	            continue
232	        try:
233	            packet = json.loads(raw)
234	        except json.JSONDecodeError:
235	            row.update({"ok": False, "error": "brief emitted no JSON", "hit": False, "prefix_fraction": 1.0})
236	            rows.append(row)
237	            continue
238	        surfaced = {str(f.get("id")) for f in packet.get("facts") or []}
239	        row["hit"] = all(fact_id in surfaced for fact_id in task["relevant"])
240	        offset = raw.find('"facts"')
241	        row["prefix_fraction"] = (offset / len(raw)) if (offset >= 0 and raw) else 1.0
242	        rows.append(row)
243	    hits = sum(1 for r in rows if r["hit"])
244	    return {
245	        "tasks": len(rows),
246	        "hit_rate": (hits / len(rows)) if rows else 0.0,
247	        "max_prefix_fraction": max((r["prefix_fraction"] for r in rows), default=1.0),
248	        "mean_bytes": (sum(r["bytes"] for r in rows) / len(rows)) if rows else 0.0,
249	        "rows": rows,
250	    }
251	
252	
253	def measure(binary: Path, label: str, workdir: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
254	    """Seed a fresh store with `binary` and measure it. Raises ProbeError on contract breaks."""
255	    facts = load_json(FACTS_PATH)
256	    tasks = load_json(TASKS_PATH)
257	    if not binary.is_file():
258	        raise ProbeError(f"{label}: binary not found at {binary}")
259	    store = FixtureStore(workdir / label, facts["origin"], facts["branch"])
260	    store.create()
261	    ids = seed(store, binary, facts)
262	
263	    expected = {fact_id for task in tasks for fact_id in task["relevant"]}
264	    seeded = set(ids.values())
265	    missing = sorted(expected - seeded)
266	    if missing:
267	        raise ProbeError(
268	            f"{label}: frozen task labels reference {len(missing)} fact id(s) the seeded store does not contain "
269	            f"(first: {missing[0]}); fact id derivation or the fixture changed, re-run `run.py freeze` deliberately"
270	        )
271	
272	    summary = eval_facts(store, binary, TASKS_PATH)
273	    results = summary.get("results") or []
274	    tight = eval_facts(store, binary, top_rank_tasks(tasks, workdir / f"{label}-top-rank-tasks.json"))
275	    brief = brief_probe(store, binary, tasks)
276	    return {
277	        "label": label,
278	        "binary": str(binary),
279	        "facts_seeded": len(ids),
280	        "tasks": summary.get("tasks", 0),
281	        "tasks_sha256": (summary.get("run_config") or {}).get("tasks_sha256"),
282	        "brain_manifest_sha256": (summary.get("run_config") or {}).get("brain_manifest_sha256"),
283	        "mean_recall": mean_recall(summary),
284	        "top_rank_hit_rate": mean_recall(tight),
285	        "mean_precision": float(summary.get("mean_precision", 0.0)),
286	        "mean_useful_per_1k": float(summary.get("mean_useful_per_1k", 0.0)),
287	        "mean_tokens": float(summary.get("mean_tokens", 0.0)),
288	        "brief_hit_rate": brief["hit_rate"],
289	        "brief_max_prefix_fraction": brief["max_prefix_fraction"],
290	        "brief_mean_bytes": brief["mean_bytes"],
291	        "per_task": [
292	            {
293	                "id": r.get("id"),
294	                "recall": r.get("recall"),
295	                "precision": r.get("precision"),
296	                "useful_per_1k": r.get("useful_per_1k"),
297	                "tokens": r.get("tokens"),
298	            }
299	            for r in results
300	        ],
301	        "brief_rows": brief["rows"],
302	    }
303	
304	
305	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
306	# scoring
307	
308	
309	def score(branch: dict[str, Any] | None, base: dict[str, Any] | None, error: str | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
310	    """Turn measurements into the trail monitor value and rationale.
311	
312	    value = 100 * min(branch mean recall, branch brief hit rate), floored to 0
313	    when the brief packet puts its facts past BRIEF_PREFIX_LIMIT of the bytes
314	    or when the measurement could not be made. Base deltas go in the rationale.
315	    """
316	    if error or branch is None:
317	        return {"value": 0, "rationale": f"Retrieval probe could not run: {error or 'no branch measurement'}"}
318	
319	    recall = branch["mean_recall"]
320	    top = branch["top_rank_hit_rate"]
321	    hit = branch["brief_hit_rate"]
322	    prefix = branch["brief_max_prefix_fraction"]
323	    value = int(round(100 * min(recall, hit)))
324	    flags: list[str] = []
325	    if prefix > BRIEF_PREFIX_LIMIT:
326	        value = 0
327	        flags.append(f"brief packet puts facts after {prefix:.0%} of its bytes (limit {BRIEF_PREFIX_LIMIT:.0%})")
328	
329	    parts = [
330	        f"facts recall@k {recall:.0%}, top-rank {top:.0%}, brief hit rate {hit:.0%}, "
331	        f"useful/1k {branch['mean_useful_per_1k']:.1f} on {branch['tasks']} frozen tasks"
332	    ]
333	    if base is not None:
334	        d_recall = recall - base["mean_recall"]
335	        d_top = top - base["top_rank_hit_rate"]
336	        d_useful = branch["mean_useful_per_1k"] - base["mean_useful_per_1k"]
337	        d_hit = hit - base["brief_hit_rate"]
338	        parts.append(
339	            f"vs base: recall {d_recall:+.0%}, top-rank {d_top:+.0%}, brief hit {d_hit:+.0%}, useful/1k {d_useful:+.1f}"
340	        )
341	        if d_recall < 0 or d_hit < 0:
342	            flags.append("branch recovers fewer labeled facts than base")
343	        elif d_top < 0:
344	            flags.append("labeled facts rank lower than on base")
345	        elif d_useful < -0.05 * max(base["mean_useful_per_1k"], 1e-9):
346	            flags.append("useful-per-1k fell more than 5% against base")
347	    if flags:
348	        parts.append("REGRESSION: " + "; ".join(flags))
349	    return {"value": value, "rationale": ". ".join(parts) + ".", "regressed": bool(flags)}
350	
351	
352	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
353	# building
354	
355	
356	def build(source: Path, output: Path) -> None:
357	    proc = run(["go", "build", "-o", str(output), "./cmd/entire-brain"], cwd=source, env=os.environ.copy(), timeout=900)
358	    if proc.returncode != 0:
359	        raise ProbeError(f"go build in {source} failed: {proc.stderr.strip()[-400:]}")
360	
361	
362	def build_base(root: Path, base_ref: str, workdir: Path) -> Path:
363	    worktree = workdir / "base-src"
364	    env = git_env(os.environ.copy())
365	    proc = run(["git", "worktree", "add", "-q", "--detach", str(worktree), base_ref], cwd=root, env=env)
366	    if proc.returncode != 0:
367	        raise ProbeError(f"git worktree add {base_ref} failed: {proc.stderr.strip()[:300]}")
368	    try:
369	        binary = workdir / "entire-brain-base"
370	        build(worktree, binary)
371	        return binary
372	    finally:
373	        run(["git", "worktree", "remove", "--force", str(worktree)], cwd=root, env=env)
374	
375	
376	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
377	# commands
378	
379	
380	def cmd_freeze(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
381	    facts = load_json(FACTS_PATH)
382	    questions = load_json(QUESTIONS_PATH)
383	    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="brain-retrieval-freeze-") as tmp:
384	        store = FixtureStore(Path(tmp) / "freeze", facts["origin"], facts["branch"])
385	        store.create()
386	        ids = seed(store, Path(args.bin).resolve(), facts)
387	    tasks = []
388	    for q in questions:
389	        unknown = [k for k in q["relevant_keys"] if k not in ids]
390	        if unknown:
391	            raise ProbeError(f"question {q['id']} names unknown fact key(s): {unknown}")
392	        tasks.append(
393	            {
394	                "id": q["id"],
395	                "task": q["task"],
396	                "branch": facts["branch"],
397	                "k": int(q.get("k", 5)),
398	                "relevant": [ids[k] for k in q["relevant_keys"]],
399	                "label_source": "human",
400	            }
401	        )
402	    TASKS_PATH.write_text(json.dumps(tasks, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
403	    print(f"wrote {TASKS_PATH} ({len(tasks)} tasks, {len(ids)} facts, {sha256_file(TASKS_PATH)})")
404	    return 0
405	
406	
407	def cmd_measure(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
408	    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="brain-retrieval-measure-") as tmp:
409	        try:
410	            report = measure(Path(args.bin).resolve(), "branch", Path(tmp))
411	            monitor = score(report, None)
412	        except ProbeError as exc:
413	            report, monitor = {"error": str(exc)}, score(None, None, str(exc))
414	    emit(report, monitor, args.json)
415	    return 0
416	
417	
418	def cmd_compare(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
419	    root = repo_root()
420	    base_ref = args.base_ref or f"origin/{args.base_branch}"
421	    report: dict[str, Any] = {"fixture": {"facts": sha256_file(FACTS_PATH), "tasks": sha256_file(TASKS_PATH)}, "base_ref": base_ref}
422	    branch_m = base_m = None
423	    error = None
424	    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="brain-retrieval-compare-") as tmp:
425	        work = Path(tmp)
426	        try:
427	            if args.branch_bin:
428	                branch_bin = Path(args.branch_bin).resolve()
429	            else:
430	                branch_bin = work / "entire-brain-branch"
431	                build(root, branch_bin)
432	            branch_m = measure(branch_bin, "branch", work)
433	            report["branch"] = branch_m
434	        except ProbeError as exc:
435	            error = str(exc)
436	            report["branch"] = {"error": error}
437	        if error is None:
438	            try:
439	                base_bin = Path(args.base_bin).resolve() if args.base_bin else build_base(root, base_ref, work)
440	                base_m = measure(base_bin, "base", work)
441	                report["base"] = base_m
442	            except ProbeError as exc:
443	                # A missing base is a weaker measurement, not a failed one.
444	                report["base"] = {"error": str(exc)}
445	    monitor = score(branch_m, base_m, error)
446	    if base_m is None and error is None:
447	        monitor["rationale"] += f" Base comparison unavailable: {report['base']['error'][:160]}."
448	    emit(report, monitor, args.json)
449	    return 0
450	
451	
452	def emit(report: dict[str, Any], monitor: dict[str, Any], compact: bool) -> None:
453	    """Report first, monitor object as the very last stdout line."""
454	    if not compact:
455	        print(json.dumps(report, indent=2))
456	    print(json.dumps({"value": monitor["value"], "rationale": monitor["rationale"]}))
457	
458	
459	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
460	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
461	    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
462	
463	    p = sub.add_parser("freeze", help="seed the fixture and write fixture/tasks.json with resolved fact ids")
464	    p.add_argument("--bin", required=True, help="entire-brain binary used to resolve fact ids")
465	    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_freeze)
466	
467	    p = sub.add_parser("measure", help="measure one binary against the frozen fixture")
468	    p.add_argument("--bin", required=True)
469	    p.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="print only the monitor line")
470	    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_measure)
471	
472	    p = sub.add_parser("compare", help="build HEAD and a base ref, measure both, print the monitor line last")
473	    p.add_argument("--base-branch", default="main", help="base branch name; the ref becomes origin/<name>")
474	    p.add_argument("--base-ref", help="explicit base ref (overrides --base-branch)")

1	# Retrieval regression probe
2	
3	> **Status: regression signal, not evidence.** This probe tells a trail whether
4	> the branch still recovers a frozen set of labeled memories as well as the base
5	> branch does. It is deterministic, unpaid, and runs in under a minute. It makes
6	> no claim about Brain's value to an agent; that lane is `../agent-brain/` and
7	> its claim gate.
8	
9	## Why it exists
10	
11	Issue #335 put a 12.8 KB status block ahead of facts in `brief --json`. Agents
12	truncated the packet, Brain went from useful to 0/3 recovered in the memory
13	ladder, and nothing on the trail noticed before merge. Every retrieval surface
14	had an offline evaluator by then; none ran per trail. This probe is the
15	missing per-trail check.
16	
17	## What it measures
18	
19	For one `entire-brain` binary:
20	
21	1. Creates a throwaway repository with a fixed origin so the brain store key is
22	   deterministic, and points the binary at throwaway plugin directories through
23	   `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_*_DIR`. Nothing touches the developer's real store.
24	2. Records every memory in `fixture/facts.json` with `remember --agent none`.
25	   Fact ids are content-derived, so the ids match `fixture/tasks.json` exactly;
26	   a mismatch is reported as a contract break, never scored as recall zero.
27	3. Runs `memories eval --retriever facts` over `fixture/tasks.json` (human
28	   labels, k=5, no judge) and reads mean recall and useful-per-1k. Precision at
29	   a fixed k is pinned near 1/k on a one-label task, so it is reported but not
30	   scored.
31	4. Runs the same eval again with k set to the number of labels per task. That
32	   recall is 1 only when every labeled fact outranks every distractor, which is
33	   the ranking signal (`top_rank_hit_rate`).
34	5. Runs `brief <task> --json` for every task and checks that the labeled facts
35	   are in the packet (brief's default limit is three facts, so this is a
36	   top-three check), plus how far into the packet the `facts` key sits.
37	
38	`compare` does this for a HEAD build and a base-ref build and reports both.
39	
40	The trail monitor value is `100 × min(mean recall, brief hit rate)`, forced to
41	0 when the brief packet puts its facts past half of its bytes (the #335 shape)
42	or when the probe cannot run at all. Deltas against base go in the rationale,
43	with a `REGRESSION:` marker when the branch recovers fewer facts than base,
44	ranks a labeled fact lower than base does, or useful-per-1k falls more than 5%.
45	
46	## What it does not measure
47	
48	- History, docs, issues or query retrievers (the fixture has no sessions).
49	- Whether an agent uses what it is given.
50	- Anything at corpus scale; the fixture is 24 memories and 22 questions.
51	- Latency, which is noise at this size.
52	
53	A branch that scores 100 here can still be a retrieval regression on a real
54	corpus. A branch that scores below base here has a regression a human should
55	look at before merge.
56	
57	## Run it
58	
59	```sh
60	python3 benchmarks/retrieval-regression/run.py compare --base-branch main
61	```
62	
63	Builds HEAD and `origin/main` with `go build`, measures both, prints a JSON
64	report and then the monitor object as the last line. Use `--branch-bin` and
65	`--base-bin` to skip the builds, `--json` for the monitor line only.
66	
67	```sh
68	python3 benchmarks/retrieval-regression/run.py measure --bin ./entire-brain
69	```
70	
71	One binary, no base comparison.
72	
73	## Change the fixture
74	
75	Edit `fixture/facts.json` or `fixture/questions.json`, then re-freeze the task
76	ids with a known-good binary and commit all three files together:
77	
78	```sh
79	python3 benchmarks/retrieval-regression/run.py freeze --bin ./entire-brain
80	```
81	
82	`tasks.json` is generated; do not hand-edit it. The runner compares the
83	seeded ids against it on every run, so a change to fact id derivation shows up
84	as a contract break with a clear message rather than a silent score drop.
85	
86	Keep distractors: several memories share vocabulary on purpose (three on
87	`brief`, three on ranking, two on scoping) so that a ranking change moves the
88	top-rank hit rate, not only recall at k.
89	
90	## The trail runner
91	
92	`.entire/runners/trail-retrieval-regression.json` runs `compare` on every push
93	and emits the monitor as `retrieval` (percent, higher is better). The sandbox
94	needs `go` and `git` with the base branch fetchable as `origin/<base>`. When
95	either is missing the probe reports value 0 with a rationale that says why;
96	read the rationale before treating a 0 as a regression.
97	
98	## Tests
99	
100	```sh
101	python3 -B -m unittest discover -s benchmarks/retrieval-regression -p 'test_*.py'
102	```
103	
104	`mise run test:benchmarks` runs the same. Scoring and fixture-contract tests run everywhere. The end-to-end test runs only when
105	`ENTIRE_BENCHMARK_BRAIN_BINARY` points at a built binary.

(Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)
- entire-search: Search Entire checkpoint history and transcripts with `entire search --json`. Use proactively when the user asks about previous work, commits, sessions, prompts, or historical context in this repository. (Tools: Bash)
- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)
- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

// cap the bytes they read from a tool call, so the sections the task needs
// (facts, history, likely files, guidance) come first and the status report,
// which is mostly provider freshness warnings and can run to 10+ KB, comes
// last. A brief that was correct but truncated before its facts section is how
// an agent misses a decision the brain had already retrieved (issue #335).
type brainBriefJSONReport struct {
	Issues             []unifiedResult             `json:"issues,omitempty"`
	GeneratedAt        time.Time                   `json:"generated_at"`
	Task               string                      `json:"task"`
	Facts              []brainBriefJSONFact        `json:"facts,omitempty"`
	GlobalFactIDs      []string                    `json:"global_fact_ids,omitempty"`
	FactsLocusDrift    map[string][]string         `json:"facts_locus_drift,omitempty"`
	FactsPendingReview map[string]factReviewNotice `json:"facts_pending_review,omitempty"`
	History            brainBriefHistory           `json:"history"`
	Conversation       []brainBriefConversationHit `json:"conversation,omitempty"`
	LikelyEditFiles    []string                    `json:"likely_edit_files,omitempty"`
	LikelyTestFiles    []string                    `json:"likely_test_files,omitempty"`
	LikelyFiles        []string                    `json:"likely_files,omitempty"`
	ActionChecklist    []brainBriefAction          `json:"action_checklist,omitempty"`
	Guidance           []string                    `json:"guidance"`
	Warnings           []string                    `json:"warnings,omitempty"`
	Semantic           brainBriefJSONSemantic      `json:"semantic"`
	Status             brainStatusReport           `json:"status"`
}

type brainBriefJSONSemantic struct {
	Context       brainBriefJSONContext   `json:"context"`
	RuntimeTraces []compactSemanticRecord `json:"runtime_traces,omitempty"`
	Tests         brainBriefJSONTests     `json:"tests"`
}

type brainBriefJSONContext struct {
	Symbols   []compactSemanticRecord `json:"symbols"`
	Relations []compactSemanticRecord `json:"relations"`
	Neighbors []compactSemanticRecord `json:"neighbors,omitempty"`

input.message:
Review of benchmarks/retrieval-regression (uncommitted) and .entire/runners/trail-retrieval-regression.json. Findings only, ranked by severity. Brain preflight: `entire brain version` = dev, capabilities report durable_facts/task_briefs/bm25_retrieval; brief and recall ran (one authored memory describing this probe, nothing contradicting the code). Source claims below are verified against the working tree, not run.

## HIGH

**1. The #335 detector is keyed on the first `"facts"` substring and the status block contains one. run.py:240-241.**
`brainStatusReport` (internal/cli/agent_surface.go:76-96) has `Facts *brainStatusFacts \`json:"facts,omitempty"\`` after only `issue_source, generated_at, integrity, repo, brain, sources`, and `brainStatusFacts` itself starts with `"facts": <count>`. If a change puts `status` ahead of the top-level `facts` (exactly the #335 shape: `brainBriefJSONReport`, agent_surface.go:303-322), `raw.find('"facts"')` lands on `status.facts` a few hundred bytes in. Probe reports prefix_fraction ~0.02, value 100, no flag. The probe misses the one regression it was written to catch. `test_status_block_before_facts_zeroes_the_value` only exercises `score()` with a hand-fed 0.8, so nothing covers this. Fix: parse with `object_pairs_hook` to get top-level key order and sum `len(json.dumps(v))` of the keys preceding `facts`, or assert `list(packet)[:3]` contains `facts`. Same line: because `facts` is `omitempty`, a packet that retrieved nothing has no key at all, which the probe reports as "brief packet puts facts after 100% of its bytes" (wrong diagnosis, see 4).

**2. The number is produced by the code under test, from inputs the PR controls. run.py:272-290, 263-270, 439-447; runner prompt.**
- Recall, top-rank and useful/1k are read straight from `memories eval` JSON (`summary["results"][i]["recall"]`), computed inside the branch binary (internal/cli/facts_eval.go:163-180, k applied at 1067-1097). A PR that changes `evalItemMetrics`, how `k` is applied, or `evalLabelsForRetriever` moves the score without touching retrieval. The probe never recomputes recall from returned ids.
- The runner executes the PR's copy of run.py, fixture/, and even the runner JSON itself. Setting `BRIEF_PREFIX_LIMIT = 2.0`, returning 100 from `score`, or editing `questions.json` so `relevant_keys` is `[]` (then `all([])` is True at run.py:239, `max(1, 0)` at :190, and `test_frozen_tasks_match_questions` still passes because it only compares lengths) all read 100. `report["fixture"]` hashes are computed (run.py:421) but never compared to anything or put in the rationale.
- Re-freezing `tasks.json` in a PR (legitimate whenever id derivation changes) makes the *base* binary fail the contract check at run.py:265-270 (its seeded ids no longer match the branch's tasks.json). That is caught as "Base comparison unavailable" (run.py:443-447) and the monitor becomes branch-alone: 100 with no REGRESSION flag possible. A PR that wants to dodge the comparison just re-freezes.
Mitigation: have the runner run `git show origin/<base>:benchmarks/retrieval-regression/run.py` (and fixture) from base for both sides, compute recall in the probe from surfaced ids (eval emits `relevant_surfaced`/`surfaced`, or use `recall --json`), and put fixture/tasks sha prefixes in the rationale so a reviewer sees them change.

**3. Base deltas never touch the value; `regressed` is dropped on the wire. run.py:323-349, 456.**
`value = 100 * min(recall, hit)` ignores `top_rank_hit_rate`, `useful_per_1k`, and `brief_mean_bytes`. A branch whose labeled facts fall from rank 1 to rank 5 on every task, or whose brief packet grows 10x, shows 100 on the trail; the only trace is "REGRESSION:" inside the rationale string, and the `regressed` boolean computed at :349 is not emitted by `emit()` at :456, so no consumer can key on it. Combined with 2: raising brief's default `--limit` from 3 to 24 makes every task a hit (all 24 fixture facts surface), bytes balloon, value 100.

## MEDIUM

**4. Tooling failures in the brief probe are reported as a retrieval regression. run.py:226-237, 325-327.**
A non-zero exit, non-JSON stdout, a renamed `facts` key, or a schema change to `facts[].id` sets `hit=False, prefix_fraction=1.0` → value 0 with rationale "REGRESSION: brief packet puts facts after 100% of its bytes (limit 50%)". The README (lines 94-96) promises a reader can tell tooling gaps from regressions; this path says the opposite of the truth and buries stderr in `brief_rows` which the monitor line does not carry. Should raise ProbeError (or a distinct flag) when any row has `ok=False` or no `facts` key.

**5. Zero labeled results reads as recall 0%, not a contract break. run.py:181-183, 283-284.**
`mean_recall` returns 0.0 when no result has `labeled: true`. If a branch tightens label policy (facts_eval.go:838-869 decides `labeled`), or eval renames `results`, value becomes 0 with "facts recall@k 0% ... REGRESSION: branch recovers fewer labeled facts than base". Same for an empty `tasks.json` (hit_rate 0, `max(..., default=1.0)` → "#335 shape"). Raise ProbeError when `len(labeled) != len(tasks)`.

**6. Environment leaks into and out of the fixture store. run.py:110, 133-140.**
`os.environ.copy()` is passed through with only the four plugin dirs, repo root, and SESSION_ID overridden.
- `ENTIRE_BRAIN_WEBHOOK_URL`: `remember` calls `notifyFactWebhook` (internal/cli/facts_write_cmd.go:236; webhooks.go says on unless `ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS`). A developer with a webhook configured POSTs 24 fixture facts per build (48 per compare) to their endpoint, with text if `ENTIRE_BRAIN_WEBHOOK_INCLUDE_TEXT` is set. Review of benchmarks/retrieval-regression (uncommitted) and .entire/runners/trail-retrieval-regression.json. Findings only, ranked by severity. Brain preflight: `entire brain version` = dev, capabilities report durable_facts/task_briefs/bm25_retrieval; brief and recall ran (one authored memory describing this probe, nothing contradicting the code). Source claims below are verified against the working tree, not run.

## HIGH

**1. The #335 detector is keyed on the first `"facts"` substring and the status block contains one. run.py:240-241.**
`brainStatusReport` (internal/cli/agent_surface.go:76-96) has `Facts *brainStatusFacts \`json:"facts,omitempty"\`` after only `issue_source, generated_at, integrity, repo, brain, sources`, and `brainStatusFacts` itself starts with `"facts": <count>`. If a change puts `status` ahead of the top-level `facts` (exactly the #335 shape: `brainBriefJSONReport`, agent_surface.go:303-322), `raw.find('"facts"')` lands on `status.facts` a few hundred bytes in. Probe reports prefix_fraction ~0.02, value 100, no flag. The probe misses the one regression it was written to catch. `test_status_block_before_facts_zeroes_the_value` only exercises `score()` with a hand-fed 0.8, so nothing covers this. Fix: parse with `object_pairs_hook` to get top-level key order and sum `len(json.dumps(v))` of the keys preceding `facts`, or assert `list(packet)[:3]` contains `facts`. Same line: because `facts` is `omitempty`, a packet that retrieved nothing has no key at all, which the probe reports as "brief packet puts facts after 100% of its bytes" (wrong diagnosis, see 4).

**2. The number is produced by the code under test, from inputs the PR controls. run.py:272-290, 263-270, 439-447; runner prompt.**
- Recall, top-rank and useful/1k are read straight from `memories eval` JSON (`summary["results"][i]["recall"]`), computed inside the branch binary (internal/cli/facts_eval.go:163-180, k applied at 1067-1097). A PR that changes `evalItemMetrics`, how `k` is applied, or `evalLabelsForRetriever` moves the score without touching retrieval. The probe never recomputes recall from returned ids.
- The runner executes the PR's copy of run.py, fixture/, and even the runner JSON itself. Setting `BRIEF_PREFIX_LIMIT = 2.0`, returning 100 from `score`, or editing `questions.json` so `relevant_keys` is `[]` (then `all([])` is True at run.py:239, `max(1, 0)` at :190, and `test_frozen_tasks_match_questions` still passes because it only compares lengths) all read 100. `report["fixture"]` hashes are computed (run.py:421) but never compared to anything or put in the rationale.
- Re-freezing `tasks.json` in a PR (legitimate whenever id derivation changes) makes the *base* binary fail the contract check at run.py:265-270 (its seeded ids no longer match the branch's tasks.json). That is caught as "Base comparison unavailable" (run.py:443-447) and the monitor becomes branch-alone: 100 with no REGRESSION flag possible. A PR that wants to dodge the comparison just re-freezes.
Mitigation: have the runner run `git show origin/<base>:benchmarks/retrieval-regression/run.py` (and fixture) from base for both sides, compute recall in the probe from surfaced ids (eval emits `relevant_surfaced`/`surfaced`, or use `recall --json`), and put fixture/tasks sha prefixes in the rationale so a reviewer sees them change.

**3. Base deltas never touch the value; `regressed` is dropped on the wire. run.py:323-349, 456.**
`value = 100 * min(recall, hit)` ignores `top_rank_hit_rate`, `useful_per_1k`, and `brief_mean_bytes`. A branch whose labeled facts fall from rank 1 to rank 5 on every task, or whose brief packet grows 10x, shows 100 on the trail; the only trace is "REGRESSION:" inside the rationale string, and the `regressed` boolean computed at :349 is not emitted by `emit()` at :456, so no consumer can key on it. Combined with 2: raising brief's default `--limit` from 3 to 24 makes every task a hit (all 24 fixture facts surface), bytes balloon, value 100.

## MEDIUM

**4. Tooling failures in the brief probe are reported as a retrieval regression. run.py:226-237, 325-327.**
A non-zero exit, non-JSON stdout, a renamed `facts` key, or a schema change to `facts[].id` sets `hit=False, prefix_fraction=1.0` → value 0 with rationale "REGRESSION: brief packet puts facts after 100% of its bytes (limit 50%)". The README (lines 94-96) promises a reader can tell tooling gaps from regressions; this path says the opposite of the truth and buries stderr in `brief_rows` which the monitor line does not carry. Should raise ProbeError (or a distinct flag) when any row has `ok=False` or no `facts` key.

**5. Zero labeled results reads as recall 0%, not a contract break. run.py:181-183, 283-284.**
`mean_recall` returns 0.0 when no result has `labeled: true`. If a branch tightens label policy (facts_eval.go:838-869 decides `labeled`), or eval renames `results`, value becomes 0 with "facts recall@k 0% ... REGRESSION: branch recovers fewer labeled facts than base". Same for an empty `tasks.json` (hit_rate 0, `max(..., default=1.0)` → "#335 shape"). Raise ProbeError when `len(labeled) != len(tasks)`.
